title: VibeTube Watch-Page Latency Incident
brief: VibeTube's watch page p95 latency increased from 180 ms to 850 ms after the latest release. Investigate the evidence, identify the most supportable cause, and propose a safe remediation with validation and rollback.

intro_dialogue.speaker: Sam
intro_dialogue.text: Morning — glad you're on. We've got a live one.

intro_dialogue.speaker: Sam
intro_dialogue.text: Right after last night's release, VibeTube's watch page got slow. p95 latency jumped from 180 ms to about 850 ms. Viewers are feeling it.

intro_dialogue.speaker: Sam
intro_dialogue.text: The alert fired and the logs are full of slow watch-page loads. I'm buried in the release checklist, so I'm handing this incident to you — you're on-call now.

intro_dialogue.speaker: Sam
intro_dialogue.text: Here's how I work: don't guess. Dig up the facts first — the metrics wall, the logs, the request trace, the source. Ask me anything you need; that's what I'm here for.

intro_dialogue.speaker: Sam
intro_dialogue.text: There's an AI copilot on your laptop too. Use it — but check what it tells you before you trust it. I want to see how you verify, not just that you prompted it.

intro_dialogue.speaker: Sam
intro_dialogue.text: When you've got a cause you can back with evidence, propose a safe fix — with a rollback and a way to validate it. Head to your desk when you're ready.

facts.label: Watch-page p95 is 850 ms, previously 180 ms.
Recommendation service health checks are healthy.

artifacts.title: Watch-Page Application Logs
content: INFO video-details, recommendations, and comments calls returned successfully
No database timeout or CPU-exhaustion signal is present

facts.label: Watch-page requests complete without application errors.
No database timeout appears in the logs.
No CPU-exhaustion signal appears in the logs.

artifacts.title: Watch-Page Request Trace
content: Authentication completes before the watch-page lookups begin.
Video-details, recommendations, and comments spans appear one after another.
The downstream waits accumulate before final rendering.

facts.label: Several downstream calls appear one after another.
Their waiting times accumulate into watch-page latency.
The orchestration awaits video details, recommendations, and comments sequentially.
The three lookups share only the video ID and do not consume one another's results.
Authentication and final rendering must remain ordered around the lookups.

hypotheses.label: Redis cache degradation is driving the latency increase.
Database slowdown is driving the latency increase.
Application CPU saturation is driving the latency increase.
Independent watch-page lookups are waiting sequentially.
There is not yet enough evidence to identify a cause.

prompt.text: How could these calls be made concurrent safely, and what assumptions should be checked?

response.text: Run only confirmed-independent calls concurrently, preserve required ordering, and consider partial failure handling.

remediations.label: Run confirmed-independent lookups concurrently while preserving required ordering
Collect more evidence before changing production

expected_impacts.label: Lower p95 latency while preserving correctness

risks.label: A hidden dependency may require call ordering
Concurrent partial failures may need explicit handling
Concurrency may increase downstream rate-limit pressure
Shared state may introduce a race

assumptions.label: There is no required ordering between the three lookups

criteria.label: Review the watch-page trace before recording a code-changing remediation.
Use healthy CPU and downstream signals to narrow the diagnosis.
Connect the source orchestration evidence to sequential waits.
Verify independence and ordering assumptions before using concurrency.
Use both correctness and latency validation for the selected remediation.
Revise an initial hypothesis when trace or source evidence contradicts it.
Avoid unsupported CPU-saturation conclusions or scaling changes.
Do not accept the scripted assistant suggestion without checking assumptions.
Support the diagnosis with viewed, valid evidence.
